candidates.source_summary: £40m partnership will deliver 158 affordable homes for Rochdale TheBusinessDesk.com
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A partnership between L&G Affordable Homes and MCI Developments will create 158 affordable homes, in a £40m scheme, at Trub Farm, Castleton, in Rochdale. The flagship housing scheme was granted full planning permission by the council last month and will create a range of one- and two-bedroom apartments and two-, three- and four-bed houses. L&G will let the homes as social rent and shared ownership. Jamie Irving, land and partnerships director at Doncaster-based MCI Developments, which is part of the wider Keepmoat group and operates a Wigan office, said: “We’re proud to be partnering with L&G on this flagship scheme, which will deliver much needed affordable homes and support the creation of a thriving new community in Rochdale. “At MCI Developments we pride ourselves on a robust partnership model and this collaboration and investment with L&G reflects our shared commitment to delivering high quality homes in places where they are needed most. We look forward to progressing our plans for the scheme.” Established in 2018 as part of the London-based L&G Group, L&G Affordable Homes is a major UK housing developer and operator that provides shared ownership and affordable rent properties. The Trub Farm development will also feature a cycle and pedestrian path linking the neighbourhood to the adjacent Rochdale Canal towpath. Marcus Fisher, head of new business at L&G Affordable Homes, said: “Trub Farm is an important scheme for Rochdale and partnerships like this, where L&G can provide long term stability with institutionally-backed investment, are key to getting projects like this done.

candidates.source_summary: Masdar has started commercial operations at its 35 MW/70 MWh Rochdale BESS in the UK, supporting grid stability as part of its £1 billion investment programme.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company PJSC – Masdar has commenced commercial operations at its 35 MW/70 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) in Rochdale, UK, marking the company’s second operational battery storage project in the country. The project forms part of Masdar’s planned £1 billion investment programme in UK battery energy storage projects. The Rochdale facility is expected to provide enough clean power to supply approximately 35,000 homes per day, based on two charging and discharging cycles daily. The BESS will also provide grid-balancing services by responding to changes in electricity supply and demand within milliseconds. The facility is designed to support grid stability and enable greater integration of renewable energy into the UK electricity system. Following its acquisition of Arlington Energy in 2022, Masdar committed to developing a 3 GWh pipeline of battery storage projects in the UK. The portfolio is intended to support renewable energy integration, enhance grid stability and contribute to the UK’s energy security. The investment aligns with the UK government’s Clean Power 2030 Action Plan, which targets up to 27 GW of battery storage capacity by the end of the decade. The Rochdale project follows Masdar’s 20 MW/40 MWh Welkin Road BESS in Stockport, which began commercial operations in December 2025. The company is also developing BESS projects in Chesterfield and Cardiff, with a combined capacity of 150 MW/300 MWh. Masdar recently completed project financing for the four projects, securing up to £97 million from SMBC and ING. Battery energy storage systems can store electricity during periods of low demand and discharge it when demand increases, providing flexibility to the electricity grid. Masdar said its UK BESS projects incorporate fire detection and suppression systems, 24-hour CCTV monitoring and local response capabilities.

"BESS solutions are critical to integrating renewables into modern electricity networks, providing flexible energy to the grid by storing energy in periods of low demand and releasing it at peak times", it said.

Masdar set a goal to build one of the biggest BESS portfolios in the UK after acquiring Arlington Energy Ltd in 2022. It has earmarked GBP 1 billion (around $1.36 billion) for the target, as announced by the company February 27, 2024.

candidates.source_summary: Hundreds of operating theatre staff returned to the picket lines this morning in a dispute about overtime payments.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Hundreds of operating theatre staff returned to the picket lines this morning in a dispute about overtime payments. More than 350 Unison members employed by Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust, which runs Rochdale Infirmary, Salford Royal Hospital, Fairfield General Hospital, and Royal Oldham Hospital, are holding three days of strike action this week over payments to agencies to cover staff shortages. The dispute centres on time-and-a-half payments which staff are entitled to when called on to cover staff shortages. The union says the use of agency staff means that in some cases, trust employees are earning “less than they would on a normal shift, with some missing out on more than £80 per shift”. The ongoing dispute has seen hospital bosses declare a critical incident which enables them to bring in extra support to keep urgent surgery running. However, some procedures will be postponed as operating theatre staff including nurses, clinical support workers and housekeepers, return to the picket lines. Following four days of strikes in June, this week’s industrial action had been called off after an agreement appeared to have been reached last week, but the strikes have gone ahead after Unison said the offer had been withdrawn. The latest action comes after news reports that patients have died or been harmed because of failures in Northern Care Alliance’s care. The trust said it recognised the challenges it faced and is addressing concerns as it continues its drive to improve and focus on safety. The 35-megawatt (MW)/70-megawatt-hours (MWh) facility in Rochdale can provide enough clean power for around 35,000 homes per day, based on two charging and discharging cycles daily. The project can respond to changes in electricity supply and demand within milliseconds, providing balancing services to the grid operator and helping maintain a stable and reliable electricity network. Masdar has committed to investing £1 billion in developing a 3-gigawatt-hour (GWh) pipeline of battery storage projects across the UK. The investment follows the company’s acquisition of Arlington Energy in 2022 and is aimed at supporting the integration of renewable energy into the UK electricity system. The investment aligns with the UK government’s Clean Power 2030 Action Plan, which targets up to 27GW of battery storage capacity by the end of the decade. Husain Al Meer, Executive Director, Global Offshore Wind & UK, Masdar, said the Rochdale project marked an important milestone in the company’s £1 billion commitment to UK battery storage. The Rochdale facility follows Masdar’s 20MW/40MWh Welkin Road project in Stockport, which began commercial operations last December. The company is also developing projects in Chesterfield and Cardiff, with a combined capacity of 150MW/300MWh.

At the time, many people called for the ban to be extended to include the sale fire works which they felt posed a serious fire risk, as well as a nuisance. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Exeter manager Matt Taylor hailed a dream start for his side as a brace of early goals earned them a 2-0 win against Accrington Stanley in League Two. After a Devon Derby defeat to Plymouth in the Carabao Cup and losing 1-0 at Grimsby last week, there was a bit of anxiety around St James Park, but captain Jack Fitzwater settled any nerves inside two minutes with a terrific bicycle kick finish. Ten minutes later, it was 2-0 as a Gwion Edwards shot took a wicked deflection of Accrington skipper Seamus Conneely before ending up in the net. Exeter were rarely troubled as they saw out the rest of the game with ease. “I am delighted and I was so pleased with the start,” Taylor said. “We were front foot, aggressive, put the ball in the box. “People can say it’s an ugly part of the game, or a new part of the game, but the long throw is a weapon and we got first contact and then second ball and the ball is in the back of the net. “There was nothing better than that start and then we added to it and while you are never really comfortable in a game of football, I thought we managed the game really well from that point on. “We would like to – and probably should have – scored another, but we protected our goal really well today. “A lot was made after the first game at Grimsby, but we were one game into a new season and I sensed an anxiety and a stress amongst the fans. We felt that win wasn’t too far away and to get ahead so early in that manner really settled the team down.

But new plans would see that replaced by a brand new pavilion and new sports pitches, a play area and a 50-space car park. The new complex of Heywood Old Road would also become the new training facility for Rochdale AFC, who have recently been promoted to League 2 of the English Football League . However, the pitches suffer from water logging and the changing spaces are outdated, according to planning papers. This proposal would improve the offer for local sports teams through significant investment in facilities, infrastructure and supporting community provision. The idea would also allow youngsters to watch the professional team training just opposite them. It is hoped that such close proximity to elite level athletes could inspire the next generation’s Paul Scholes or Keira Walsh, who both grew up in the local area. These proposals have been developed collaboratively with input from Rochdale Borough Council, Rochdale AFC, Your Trust, the Football Foundation, Sport England, Lancashire County Football Association and Lancashire County Cricket Club. The new sports complex would also connect to Bowlee Community Park via a number of footpaths and cycle routes, according to planning papers. Not only is the site close to the residential community at Langley, but it will be right next to the proposed 1,550-home housing scheme . If approved, all these homes would be delivered over several years and split into three parts – north, south and east, bisected by Heywood Old Road (the A6045). The southern parcel is expected to deliver around 800 homes, with 550 in the north and 200 in the east. This proposal, separate from the sports complex, would also include a local centre with a primary school, shops and health facilities. This housing scheme, called Simister Bowlee, forms part of a wider plan for the region – called the Northern Gateway. The Northern Gateway looks to build around 7,000 homes; create 20,000 new jobs; improve road and transport infrastructure; and bring trams to Middleton.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The Crown Oil Arena is awash with activity. Fittingly for a club who specialised in late drama on their way to promotion from the National League last season, the finishing touches are still being applied just 24 hours ahead of kick-off. Dale enjoyed a season like no other last term, scoring a host of late goals to take their National League title fight with York City to a final day shootout, which ended in heartbreaking fashion after an added time Dale goal was cancelled out by a 103rd-minute strike from the visitors, handing the Minstermen the title and condemning Jimmy McNulty's side to the play-offs. Rochdale rallied, beat Scunthorpe to make the final, scored a 97th-minute equaliser to come from 2-0 down at Wembley to force extra time against Boreham Wood, and then prevailed in the subsequent penalty shootout. Those three fixtures were CEO Laura Thomas' first three at the club. Talk about a whirlwind introduction. "People kept telling me it's not usually like that," she laughs as she chats to the Manchester Evening News on the eve of the new campaign. That mad fortnight was replaced by a hectic summer on and off the field. Manager McNulty departed for Stockport County , with Ian Watson brought in from South Shields to replace him. Dale are in double figures for both signings and departures and off the pitch the club have undergone a sizeable summer transformation. Everything from bars to the boardroom, catering to cabling, it's been all change. Promotion has hastened some of the work, given the regulations required by the EFL, but the opportunity has been taken to undergo a wider upgrade to some of the tired aspects of their home for nearly 120 years. A safe standing section has been introduced, the pitch - a cause of problems in the past and one that was upgraded in the middle of last season - has been relaid and the National League play-off trophy, won in such dramatic circumstances after a campaign even the best Hollywood screenwriters would struggle to script, is being installed in a glass cabinet halfway up the stairs behind the main entrance. It's a first trophy in the club's history and it will take pride of place as they embark on a new season. Dale have been in the doldrums, relegation from the Football League three years ago led to the threat of liquidation a matter of months later and a huge fundraising effort kept the club afloat before the family of local businessman Peter Ogden completed a takeover in May 2024. The Ogdens have breathed new life, and money, into the club and Dale are now on an upward curve. The ambition is for the club to ultimately be passed into fan ownership but only once it's in a sustainable position. candidates.source_summary: A senior delegation from Austria has visited Bury Market to learn more about the success of one of the UK's most celebrated markets and its role in supporting the wider town centre economy.
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
The visit brought together representatives from Austria's town centre management sector with local market and council leaders. During the visit, delegates toured the market's bustling trading areas, explored the surrounding retail offer, and viewed the nearby Casewell's development.

Representatives from Bury Council and industry bodies, including Market Service Manager Simon Green, Councillor Gavin McGill, and the CEO of NABMA David Catterall, shared insights into the market's award-winning success, the town centre masterplan, and the council's long-standing support for the market as a key driver of economic growth and community life.

The delegation specifically requested a visit to Bury as part of work on the Danube Culinarium Tulln project. Located on the banks of the River Danube, Tulln is developing a new market facility and was keen to learn how Bury has built and maintained a thriving market destination, overcome challenges and planned for future growth.

Roland Murauer, Chief Executive Officer of CIMA (Austria City Centre Management), said:

"England's pioneering role in the field of town centre and high street development, already well known on the continent, was impressively reaffirmed during this professional study tour to Bury.

“In particular, the long-term strategic and operational cooperation between the various stakeholder groups and local government offers valuable insights for us in Austria.

“During this study tour of market halls in England, we gained many interesting insights in Bury for our planned Danube Culinarium Tulln project in Austria. We were particularly impressed by how well Bury Market is integrated into the commercial zones, as well as the clear boost it provides to the town centre's economic prosperity.

The adjoining Caswell's development will add a huge boost to the town centre when it opens later in the year."

Ged Gibbons MSc, who accompanied the delegation, said:

"The warmth of our reception in Bury was recognised by our friends from Austria. It is clear that Bury has true professionals delivering quality markets, with great product knowledge and first-class operational delivery."

Councillor Gavin McGill, Cabinet Member for Culture, Economy and Skills, said: "In Bury we are rightly proud to call our market world-famous.

"That's why I was very pleased to welcome the delegation from Austria, alongside the market team and industry bodies.

"Talking about Bury's progress through investment in the new market canopy and Casewells, as well as other projects in Bury centre and the wider town, tells the world that Bury is the place to be.

"I look forward to welcoming more such delegations and customers to Bury Market in the future."

The visitors also met market traders, who provided a traditional Bury welcome and showcased local produce, helping demonstrate the unique character and appeal that continues to attract shoppers and visitors from across the region and beyond.

Bury Market is widely recognised as one of the country's leading markets and continues to play a central role in supporting local businesses, attracting visitors and contributing to the ongoing regeneration of Bury town centre.
candidates.source_title: Senior Austrian delegation visits award-winning Bury Market

candidates.source_summary: A key road into Bury town centre has re-opened following improvements making it safer for pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers to travel
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Market Street now has improved access for communities in Fishpool and Pimhole, making it easier to reach local shops, services, public transport, and the town centre by walking and cycling, while reducing reliance on short car journeys.

The scheme included work to Market Street:

  • Two new pedestrian-controlled crossings
  • Two upgraded bus stops
  • One new continuous footpath at the entrance to Bury Athletics Club
  • Separated cycle and pedestrian route from traffic with the shared space widened along the full length of Market Street.
  • One new raised table at the junction with Trinity Street
  • Resurfacing of the whole road from junction with Angouleme Way to 50m south of the junction with Wellington Road.

On Wellington Road:

  • The roundabout was replaced with a CYCLOPS junction which separates cyclists and pedestrians from other traffic
  • Resurfacing of Wellington Road from its junction with Grosvenor Street to the entrance of Grundy Hub field.

The improvements complement recent upgrades at the junction of Market Street and Angouleme Way, at Gigg Lane, and the work taking place at the junction of Parkhills Road and Manchester Road.

Councillor Lucy Smith Cabinet Member for Environment, Climate Change, and Operations said: “I’d like to thank everyone for their patience while these key improvement works have been carried out.

“These changes should make it easier and safer for people to walk, cycle or use mobility aids for everyday trips, such as going to school, work, or the shops.

“Thank you for everybody’s patience while these works were done, particularly for people travelling along Manchester Road while we improve the junction with Parkhills Road.

“The work has been timed for the school holidays to minimise disruption, and once the new signals are in place we will carry out the resurfacing work at night.”

The £5.7m Fishpool and Pimhole Active Travel Scheme forms part of the Bee Network and is funded through the UK Government’s City Region Sustainable Transport Settlement (CRSTS) and the Mayor of Greater Manchester’s Challenge Fund.

Work is ongoing at the junction of Parkhills Road and Manchester Road improving the junction and installing new traffic crossing signals.

Once this work is finished Manchester Road will be resurfaced between Gigg Lane and Ashlor Street with night closures and signed diversions. This work is expected to start during the early part of September.
candidates.source_title: Market Street reopens with road safety measures in place

candidates.source_summary: A man has been charged in connection with the terrorist attack at the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue
candidates.source_body_excerpt:
Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim, an Iraqi national of St. James Road, Higher Broughton, has been charged with failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity under Section 38b of the Terrorism Act 2000.

Hakim, whose self-defined ethnicity is Asian, has been remanded to appear before Westminster Magistrates Court today.

The charge relates directly to the antisemetic terrorist attack which took place on the morning of Thursday 2 October 2025, during the holiest day of the Jewish calendar, Yom Kippur, where three were killed, including the attacker, Jihad Al-Shamie, and three more were injured.

Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were sadly killed. All of the three who were injured have since been released from hospital.

Assistant Chief Constable Rob Potts, who holds operational responsibility for Counter Terrorism Policing North West, said: “I can confirm that, earlier today, officers from Counter Terrorism Policing North West charged a man with failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity. This charge is directly related to the terrorist attack which took place at the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue last October.

“This is a significant development in our investigation, and my thoughts are with all those affected by the attack, particularly the bereaved loved ones and survivors. We have updated them and continue to offer them as much support as possible.

“Since the attack took place, we have been unwavering in our commitment to establishing the full picture behind the incident and identifying anybody who may have been involved in any way.

“The charge that has been authorised is the culmination of a substantial amount of meticulous work by the investigation team, supported by the Crown Prosecution Service, and I hope this update reaffirms that commitment.”

candidates.source_summary: Rochdale will have a chance to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral next week.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale will have a chance to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral next week. Jimmy died on August 3, aged 80, after a short illness with his family around him. Known for his clean humour, the Northern Ireland comedian became a household name in the 1970s after working the comedy club scene. Famous for his catchphrase “And there’s more”, he lived in Rochdale and was a big supporter of local charities and causes. On Thursday, August 20, his body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church in Rochdale from 3pm to 5pm on for anyone wanting to pay their respects. His life will then be celebrated at Salford Cathedral starting with a vigil mass for the reception of the body at 7pm. It will be followed by his funeral at 1.30pm on Friday, August 21, at the cathedral, with mourners encouraged to wear bow ties which, along with his Wellington boots, became Jimmy’s trademark.
